messages:
jordan: Hi support — after rotating our API key in Vault yesterday, our EU worker fleet is getting 403s to Redwood API. Started ~15:20 UTC, ~20% of requests failing. Example curl attached.

jordan: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden *
{"error":"invalid_api_key"}

maria: sorry about that. can you confirm where the worker reads the key from? env var, file, sidecar?

jordan: it's a vault-agent sidecar rendering /etc/creds/redwood.key (Go app reads file at startup). vault wrote a new secret at secret/data/redwood/apikey-v2 and we updated template to point there.

aj: two quick suspects: 1) file update strategy preserved inode so app didn't notice change, 2) long-lived TCP keepalive connections with old header cached in clients. can you paste vault-agent template config?

jordan: here's template (redacted):
```
template {
  destination = "/etc/creds/redwood.key"
  contents = "{{ with secret "secret/data/redwood" }}{{ .Data.data.key }}{{ end }}"
}
```

vault-agent-bot: note: default behavior writes file by opening, writing, and closing which can keep inode. use `rename = true` to atomically replace file (updates inode). also `wrap_ttl` and `cache` options affect re-render frequency.

kevin: also check if the Go client caches key on init and never re-reads file — if sidecar replaces file in-place, inode same => no file watcher event. restarting process or adding file watch solves. to test quickly: `cat /etc/creds/redwood.key` on failing node; then `sudo systemctl restart myapp` and retry curl.

maria: can you run `lsof /etc/creds/redwood.key` and `stat -c '%i %U %G %n' /etc/creds/redwood.key` before and after rotation to confirm inode change?

jordan: ran checks: inode same before/after. lsof shows pid 2145 has file open. restarted app on one host and that host stopped returning 403s.

aj: confirms root cause. mitigation options: - set `rename = true` in template block, - enable Vault Agent polling/inotify (or `use_inotify` if supported), - modify app to re-read on SIGHUP or watch file, or - restart service during rotation window.

maria: we'll send a small patch for the template config and recommend a rolling restart plan. can you share exact Vault Agent version and app signal handling?

jordan: vault-agent 1.12.1, app does not watch file (reads at startup). rolling restart planned. thanks.

kevin: FYI for future: also consider client connection pool drain to avoid sticky keepalives: send a graceful restart or call an endpoint to force new connections so new Authorization header is used.

maria: closing loop — recommended KB entry added: 'vault-agent template rename=true for on-disk secret swapping' :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks all, rolling now. will report back if anything else.
